principles.notes: The repair lives entirely in app/frontend/src/lib (exportMarkdown.ts) as a pure citation-to-Markdown function with no new imports, no state, no I/O, and no network. frontend-lib has allowed_imports: [] in .factory/architecture.json and the design adds zero import edges; no formatting behavior leaks into components (ChatArea, Message, CitationModal) or hooks.

The design extends the existing deep seam formatCitation in place rather than adding a parallel formatter, a wrapping helper, or a one-off abstraction beside it. Callers (formatSources at exportMarkdown.ts:63, ChatArea.handleExport) continue to pass a Citation and receive a finished Markdown list entry with no orchestration on their side. The repair actually deepens the module: today the interface silently emits two different entry shapes across branches (marker-less degraded returns vs '- '-prefixed success paths); after the fix the contract is uniform — every non-empty-snippet entry starts with '- ', carries the '— <range>' tail, and ends with the '> "snippet"' blockquote — so a caller can reason about the output from the interface alone, which is exactly the deep-module test.
planned_files contains no backend paths; routes/db/rag/llm/services are untouched.

No trust-root paths (factory_kernel, .factory, harness, scripts/factory_*, tests/factory) are in planned_files. Independent validation observed: this governor re-verified the designer's factual claims against the working tree (current degraded return strings at exportMarkdown.ts:32, :46, :53; formatSources join semantics at :63; existing assertions at exportMarkdown.test.ts:215-227, 229-235, 260-272) instead of accepting builder reasoning, and confirmed design.json's contract_sha256 equals the validated contract sha256 3a3d954d075b96d0a73f70514823e3061337cb6def442b00d3f8f584e164df93.

rationale: The design names the seam (app/frontend/src/lib/exportMarkdown.ts#formatCitation), keeps all behavior behind it, and changes exactly three return statements plus assertions in the existing test file — planned_files match the issue's 'Files expected to change' list with zero new files and zero new imports, so the frontend-lib layer (allowed_imports: []) stays closed and no new dependency edge or cycle can arise. I verified against the working tree that the claimed deficiency is real and exactly characterized: the two YouTube fallback returns (lines 46 and 53, 'new URL()' throwing and missing-v) emit '<title> (timestamp link unavailable) — <range>' with neither the '- ' marker nor the snippet blockquote, and the Dynamous empty-lesson_url return (line 32) keeps the blockquote but lacks the marker; because formatSources newline-joins entries, the marker-less entries merge into the previous list item when rendered, and the dropped blockquote violates MISSION.md's rich-citations bar for exports. The repair is additive and preserves every currently-passing assertion I could find: the invalid-URL test's exact console.warn payload and '(timestamp link unavailable)' wording, the no-v test's no-link assertion, and the Dynamous fallback test's not-contains-(](') plus blockquote assertions all remain satisfied once '- ' is prefixed and the '\n  > "<snippet>"' shape (reusing the success-path two-space indent) is appended. The RED prediction is honest: on the unchanged tree the current suite is green and AC-1/AC-2 fail against the 'not-a-url' return (no blockquote, no leading '- '), AC-3's starts-with fails against the Dynamous return — the promised symptom '(timestamp link unavailable) — 0:10–0:20' will surface verbatim in vitest's received output provided the tests assert on the returned string with toMatch/toContain rather than boolean coercion; that condition is already pinned by the design's invariants and is bound here as a requirement of this proceed. Over a multi-ticket horizon this converges the architecture: the formatCitation interface becomes total and uniform (every surviving entry is a self-consistent Markdown list item carrying its snippet), which removes a silent trap for the already-flagged follow-up tickets (the empty-snippet guard oddity, the missing is_cited two-tier Sources rendering — correctly deferred to their own issues rather than bundled), and it demonstrates the right instinct of repairing the deep seam instead of the no-growth component that calls it. No cross-layer coupling is added, no parallel abstraction is created beside an established seam, no debt-listed hotspot is touched, and no active migration is worked against; exportMarkdown.ts is not itself in the debt registry, so its few-byte growth carries no no-growth constraint. Decision: proceed.
